answer: A single identity may take at most 19% of an epoch's reward pool; anything above the cap is repooled or burned. The kernel cap is applied at the ocean settlement and visible in the signal breakdown, which turns a pooling attack into a slow, expensive and publicly visible grind. Because of that, capturing the pool demands several independent identities, and each of them needs its own established standing, which only comes from passing graded work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
